content: 1. Rama Rao, S., Lacuest, M., Costello, M., Pangolibay, B., and Jones, H. explored the relationship between the quality of care and contraceptive use in their study published in International Family Planning Perspectives in 2003 (Volume 29, Issue 2, Pages 76–83). 2. Sanogo, D., Rama Rao, S., Johnes, H., N’diaye, P. M’bow B., and Diop, C. B. investigated strategies to improve the quality of care and contraceptive use in Senegal, as detailed in their 2003 publication in the African Journal of Reproductive Health (Volume 7, Pages 57–73). 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the second edition of its technical and policy guidance on safe abortion for health systems in 2012, providing comprehensive recommendations for improving access and safety. 4. Guyatt, G. H., Oxman, A. D., Vist, G. E., Kunz, R., Falck-Ytter, Y., Alonso-Coello, P., and colleagues introduced the GRADE system, which establishes a consensus on rating the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations, as published in BMJ in 2008 (Volume 336, Pages 924–926). 5. Schunemann, H. J., Oxman, A. D., Brozek, J., Glasziou, P., Bossuyt, P., Chang, S., and others applied the GRADE framework to assess the quality of evidence for diagnostic recommendations, as described in Evidence-Based Medicine in 2008 (Volume 13, Pages 162–163). 6. Jaeschke, R., Guyatt, G. H., Dellinger, P., Schunemann, H., Levy, M. M., Kunz, R., and colleagues discussed the use of the GRADE grid to facilitate decision-making in clinical practice guidelines when consensus is difficult to achieve, as published in BMJ in 2008 (Volume 337, Article a744). 7. Barbui, C., Dua, T., van Ommeren, M., Yasamy, M. T., Fleischmann, A., Clark, N., and others highlighted the challenges of developing evidence-based recommendations using the GRADE approach, particularly in the context of mental, neurological, and substance use disorders, as published in PLoS Medicine in 2010 (Volume 7, Issue 8, Article e1000322). 8. The United Nations Committee on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights issued General Comment No. 20 during its 42nd session, emphasizing non-discrimination in economic, social, and cultural rights under Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (CESCR). 9. Paul Hunt, the Special Rapporteur on the Right to Health, presented a report to the 60th session of the Commission on Human Rights in 2004, addressing the right of everyone to enjoy the highest attainable standard of physical and mental health. 10. The United Nations adopted the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) in 1979, which remains a cornerstone for advancing gender equality and protecting women's rights globally. 11. The United Nations Human Rights Committee issued General Comment No. 19 in 1990, focusing on the protection of the family, the right to marriage, and equality between spouses. 12. The Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 2006, emphasizing the rights and dignity of individuals with disabilities. 13. The International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (CESCR), adopted in 1966, outlines the obligations of states to uphold these rights, including the right to health. 14. The United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child issued General Comment No. 3 in 2003, addressing the rights of children in the context of HIV/AIDS. 15. The WHO's 17th Model List of Essential Medicines provides a comprehensive guide to essential medications, ensuring equitable access to critical treatments. 16. The WHO published a fact sheet on emergency contraception (Fact Sheet No. 244), offering evidence-based information on its use and accessibility. 17. The United Nations Commission on Population and Development adopted Resolution 2012/1, focusing on adolescents and youth, during its 45th session. 18. The WHO, in collaboration with UNFPA and UNICEF, developed a framework in 2006 to accelerate action for the sexual and reproductive health of young people. 19. The United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child issued General Comment No. 4 in 2003, addressing adolescent health and development within the framework of the Convention on the Rights of the Child. 20. The WHO published guidelines in 2011 on sexual and reproductive health core competencies in primary care, emphasizing the integration of these services into health systems. 21. Faden, R. R., and Beauchamp, T. L. provided a historical and theoretical analysis of informed consent in their book published by Oxford University Press in 1986. 22. The WHO released a global handbook for family planning providers in 2011, offering updated guidance on best practices. 23. Desjardins, M. examined the intersection of disability, sexuality, and sterilization in the context of intellectual disabilities, as discussed in the book Sex and Disability (Duke University Press, 2012). 24. The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics published ethical guidelines in 2011 for managing gynecological issues in severely disabled women. 25. The Council of Europe adopted the Convention on Human Rights and Biomedicine in Oviedo in 1997, addressing ethical issues in biology and medicine. 26. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) published a practical plan in 2005 to achieve the Millennium Development Goals, emphasizing the importance of investing in development. 27. The WHO's 2013 report, Women’s and Children’s Health: Evidence of Impact of Human Rights, highlights the role of human rights in improving health outcomes. 28. The United Nations Human Rights Council issued technical guidance in 2013 on applying a human rights-based approach to reducing preventable maternal morbidity and mortality. 29. The WHO's Commission on Information and Accountability for Women’s and Children’s Health released its first progress report in 2012, detailing the implementation of recommendations. 30. The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Basic Principles and Guidelines on the Right to a Remedy and Reparation for Victims of Gross Violations of International Human Rights Law in 2005. 31. Bueno de Mesquita, J., and Hunt, P. emphasized the human rights responsibilities of donors in providing international assistance and cooperation in sexual and reproductive health, as published by the University of Essex Human Rights Centre in 2008.
